newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen firm, underpinned above 126.60.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen firm, underpinned above 126.60.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract is likely to stay at around 127.00 on Monday, traders said.

They said downside room would likely be limited to around 126.60 by expected falls in Tokyo stocks after large losses on Wall Street on Friday. At the same time it would be difficult for the contract to exceed 127.34, an all-time high for any benchmark, they said.
"The market can't be totally bullish as falls in stocks may trigger investor profit-taking in JGBs ahead of end-September half-year book closings," said a dealer at a securities house.
The September ended at 126.83 in Tokyo on Friday. Its later close on LIFFE was at 126.89.

The contract hit a nearly four-month high of 127.08 on Friday, mainly on short-covering ahead of a shift in benchmark status to December later this month. But it failed to rise further amid a lack of participants during the summer holiday season, traders said.

"Since investors are back, we have to ask them if they are willing to buy new 10-year JGBs with a (record low) coupon rate of 2.3 percent (when an auction is held next week)," a dealer at another brokerage house said.
